spec.title: Config and schema: the two files, variables, validation and hot reload
spec.purpose: Every tunable is a key in one JSON file with a schema beside it; the executor's verb table is a second file. The loader resolves variables, refuses a missing or unknown key by name, validates at start, and reloads the tables while running.

section.title: What the config domain decides

node.title: scheduler/config/scheduler.json and executor.json: every tunable of the scheduler and the verb table of the executor, validated by the schemas beside them, variables resolved at load, no default in Go

section.text: In: the two files and the tables they name. Out: one typed configuration value every domain reads, and a reload signal with the new table versions. The repository lint validates the files against their schemas on every change.

section.title: The files
section.text: scheduler.json in the scheduler's config directory, with scheduler.schema.json beside it: the scheduler's own settings and the paths of the tables it reads.
executor.json with executor.schema.json beside it: the socket, the host paths, the seat the record verb writes as, and the verb table.

The tables stay where they are and keep their schemas: the routes table, the policies table, the flow configuration's gates, the role files. The scheduler reads them by the paths its own file names and never carries a copy.
The repository lint validates every config file that has a schema beside it, so the two new files are covered by the existing step with no lint change.

section.title: Variables
section.text: A string value may carry repo, state_dir, host_repo, HOME or ENV:NAME in the variable form; the loader resolves them after the file is read, and an unknown variable or an unset environment name is exit 3 naming it.

repo is the repository as mounted in the container, for reading; host_repo is the repository on the host, for the executor. The scheduler uses host_repo only in text typed or run on the host, such as a wake line's playbook path.
No absolute path, host name or user name inside the file: every machine-specific value comes in through a variable, so the file can be lifted to another host or to object storage unchanged.

section.title: No defaults, no unknown keys
section.text: A key the scheduler reads and the file lacks is exit 3 naming the key. A key the file carries and the scheduler does not know is exit 3 naming the key. Go holds no fallback value for any key.
A silent default is a literal nobody can find; the supervisor's fourteen literals were the last time this was learned.

section.title: Validation at start
section.text: Shape: every key present with its type, ranges that the schema states, mode one of off, shadow, active.

Cross checks: every role has an acknowledgement window; every gate kind has a stall deadline; poll plus the smallest deadline stays within the visible bound; every root pattern resolves to at least one directory.
The tables are loaded and checked by their own domains at start; a failure there is exit 3 with the file, the row and the key.

The verbs the scheduler can emit are a fixed list in the executor domain; the executor's Health names the verbs its table holds, and a missing one blocks going active rather than failing at the first job.

section.title: Hot reload of the tables
section.text: The routes table, the policies table, the flow gates and the role files reload while running: each tick compares the file's size and modification time, re-reads a changed file, runs its domain's checks, and swaps it in whole or not at all.
A changed file that fails its checks is kept out: the loaded table stays, one 500 note names the file and the reason, latched by file name until a later change loads.
scheduler.json and executor.json do not reload; a change to either is a restart of the process it configures, because the socket, the roots and the mode are not things to swap under running jobs.
The Reload call forces the comparison now and answers with the versions loaded.

section.title: The key registry of scheduler.json
section.key: The file's schema version.
What the scheduler may do; a variable so the run wrapper can set it from the environment.
The scheduler's own seat name on the records it writes.
The herdr session the executor addresses; carried to the executor's configuration too.
The repository as mounted for reading.
The repository on the host, for text typed or run there.
The state directory: ledger, jobs, latches, belt, shadow.
The tables.
Role files and playbooks; playbooks_dir is a host path on the wake line.
The halt flag file and the shutdown grace.
Intake's keys.

key.name: seat.busy_regex, seat.done_regex, seat.read_lines, seat.cap_wait_seconds, seat.absent_wait_seconds, seat.idle_seconds
key.type: string, string, integer, integer, integer, integer

section.key: The seats domain's keys.
The default retry policy.
Concurrency and retention.
Confirmation windows per role and re-sends.
Stall deadlines per gate kind and the visibility bound.
The heartbeat.
The executor socket as mounted in the container, the dial timeout, the health interval.
The scheduler's own socket for status, reload, drain and retry.
The lowest code that raises a herdr notification.
The periods.
Where shadow decisions go and how many agreeing records parity needs.
The log level.

section.title: The key registry of executor.json
section.key: The file's schema version.
The unix socket path the executor listens on, under the runtime directory variable.
Host paths and the session every herdr verb addresses.
The seat the record verb forces on every record it writes; the scheduler cannot override it.
How many lines of stdout and stderr come back in a verdict.
The verb table: argv template, timeout seconds, final exit codes, the allowed flag set for the record verb.
Environment names removed before every verb, the pane identity of the executor's own pane among them, so a herdr call never targets the executor's pane by accident.

section.title: Cases the build ticket proves

case.expected: exit 0: a file lacking one key fails with exit 3 and the key's dotted name in the error
exit 0: a file with an extra key fails naming it
exit 0: repo, state_dir, host_repo, HOME and ENV names resolve; an unknown variable or unset name fails naming it
exit 0: a role without an acknowledgement window, a gate kind without a deadline, and a broken visible bound each fail naming the key
exit 0: a changed valid table is swapped with a new version; a changed invalid one leaves the old version in place with one note
configs: schema ok, with scheduler.json and executor.json validated against their schemas

section.case: The repository lint covers the files.

example.text: intake.roots holds the repo variable followed by the events directory, and a second pattern over the slot pool under the HOME variable; the run wrapper mounts both read-only.
An operator adds a routes row and saves; the next tick loads it, the log says routes loaded with the new hash, and the next record uses it.
poll := cfg.PollSeconds; if poll == 0 then poll = 10.
example.why: A default nobody can find; the key is required or the file is wrong.
